name: R1b1a1b1a2a (DF13)
description: R1b-DF13 is an intermediate node between P312 and the Atlantic Celtic subclades, most notably L21. It encompasses the core of the Atlantic Bell Beaker paternal ancestry that spread across Northwestern Europe — particularly Ireland, Britain, Brittany, and the western fringe of the continent. DF13 is almost exclusively a Northwestern European lineage and is largely absent from Southern and Eastern Europe. Its expansion coincides precisely with the Bell Beaker phenomenon and the early Bronze Age transformation of the British Isles, where it effectively replaced the vast majority of pre-existing Neolithic male lineages within a few centuries.
interestingFact: Ancient DNA from Bell Beaker-associated burials in Britain dated to ~2400–1800 BCE shows that DF13-bearing individuals replaced over 90% of the male ancestry present in Britain just generations earlier, in what remains one of the most abrupt and near-total paternal replacements documented anywhere in prehistoric Europe.

clans.name: Atlantic Celts
clans.note: DF13 is the defining paternal node of the Atlantic Celtic world — the peoples who maintained Celtic languages in Ireland, Scotland, Wales, and Brittany

references: Olalde et al. (2018) — The Beaker phenomenon and the genomic transformation of northwest Europe. Nature 555, 190–196.
Cassidy et al. (2016) — Neolithic and Bronze Age migration to Ireland and establishment of the insular Atlantic genome. PNAS 113(2), 368–373.
Busby et al. (2012) — The peopling of Europe and the cautionary tale of Y chromosome lineage R-M269. Proceedings of the Royal Society B 279(1730), 884–892.
